body: Red Velvet’s Joy and Kim Hyun Jin are showing a gentler side of their characters’ relationship in new stills from “One-of-a-Kind Romance.”

The images show Gong Yu Il, played by Joy, at the home of top star Tak Mu I, played by Kim Hyun Jin. She watches over him as he sleeps looking pale and prepares an ice pack for him, though she also appears flustered to find herself in his house, Soompi reported.

Based on a webtoon, the drama follows job seeker Gong Yu Il as she unexpectedly becomes Tak Mu I’s manager. The star carries emotional scars from a stalking incident, while a novel Gong Yu Il wrote years earlier helped him find the strength to keep going.

Their first encounters were far from warm. Troubled by a stalker, Tak Mu I grew suspicious of Gong Yu Il because she repeatedly crossed paths with him. His accusations left her bewildered and put the two at odds.

His attitude shifted when he learned that she had the unpublished third volume of “Star and Half Moon,” a novel that had comforted him amid the pressures of his entertainment career. But another careless comment, comparing the scent of her hair perfume to his stalker’s, caused Gong Yu Il to close herself off again.
Episodes 3 and 4 will reveal how Gong Yu Il comes to look after Tak Mu I. They are set to be released on November 16 at 6 p.m. KST on TVING, Viu and ABEMA.

The second installment of the 2024 drama Crash follows the Traffic Crime Investigation team, or T.C.I., as it moves from Namgang Police Station to a regional unit under the National Office of Investigation. The expanded team will handle traffic crime cases across the country.

In the new images, Lee's Cha Yeon Ho and Kwak's Min So Hee visit an unusual scene during their investigation. Cha also appears to encounter someone he knows at a research institute, raising questions about how the acquaintance might be connected to the team's first case.

items.headline: Five K-Dramas to Explore After Make Me Tingle
items.dek: From legal mysteries to palace romance, Soompi's watch list offers more stories for fans of Nam Ji Hyun and Kim Jae Yeong.
body: Fans missing Nam Ji Hyun and Kim Jae Yeong after Make Me Tingle have several options for their next watch. In a recent list, Soompi highlighted five dramas that share a cast connection or explore themes of relationships and desire.

In Make Me Tingle, Nam plays marketing executive Gong Yeon Su opposite Kim as Dokgo Dal. Their romance follows two people whose views on love have been shaped by their upbringings, while leaving room for comedy and self-discovery.

For more of Nam, Suspicious Partner pairs her with Ji Chang Wook in a romance with a legal mystery at its center. Nam plays Eun Bong Hee, a former taekwondo athlete and legal professional framed for murder. She eventually works with prosecutor No Ji Wook, played by Ji, and their clashes give way to a deeper bond.

Both Make Me Tingle leads also appear in the historical drama 100 Days My Prince. Nam stars as Hong Shim, who enters an unexpected marriage with an amnesiac crown prince played by Doh Kyung Soo. Kim plays her older brother Seok Ha, who becomes involved in a conspiracy against the prince.

Kim takes on another romantic role in Love in Contract, playing a popular actor who asks a professional contract wife, played by Park Min Young, to pose as his spouse. Her long-standing client, played by Ko Kyung Pyo, is also drawn into the story.

Soompi's other picks include a murder mystery in which Kim plays idol Do Ra Ik, whose lawyer and biggest fan is played by Sooyoung. The list also recommends a series starring Hani and Woo Hee as friends who host a podcast about intimacy and desire.

items.headline: Jun Ji Hyun and Ahn Hyo Seop Review Offers for Intimate Strangers Sequel
items.dek: The actors are considering roles in a follow-up to the 2018 Korean film, with production preparations expected to begin soon.
body: Jun Ji Hyun and Ahn Hyo Seop are considering offers to star in Intimate Strangers 2, a sequel to the 2018 Korean film, Soompi reported.

Their agencies, PEACHY COMPANY and THE PRESENT COMPANY, each confirmed that their actor had received an offer and was reviewing it. The statements followed a November 16 report by MyDaily that the two would appear in the film.

The sequel follows four couples whose phones begin ringing after they connect to an advanced AI home system. As the evening unfolds, hidden truths emerge, with jealousy and feelings of inferiority driving desires that continue beyond the game.

Jun has reportedly been offered the role of Jung Yoon Ah, a beauty influencer and brand CEO determined to protect her seemingly perfect life. Ahn's proposed character is a younger media artist romantically involved with Jung Yoon Ah.

The original Intimate Strangers drew approximately 5.29 million moviegoers after its 2018 release. Directed by Lee Jae Gyu and written by Bae Se Young, the black comedy was a remake of the 2016 Italian film Perfect Strangers.

The sequel is expected to enter pre-production soon, with filming planned for early next year. Jun is currently wrapping filming on the upcoming JTBC drama Human X Gumiho, while Ahn is starring in the JTBC drama Final Table.

Based on a webtoon, the series follows Jung after an unexpected accident leaves him with a special ability. His new job brings him to Dukchun High School, where the baseball team has spent years falling out of major competitions in the preliminary rounds.

As Soompi reports, the teaser begins with Jung confident in his ability to recognize talent. His assessment of the Dukchun players quickly tests that confidence, and he struggles to conceal his frustration with their skills.

body: Ju Ji Hoon is preparing to start his own company after ending his exclusive contract with Blitzway Entertainment, the agency announced on November 16.

In a statement reported by Soompi, Blitzway said the two sides decided to conclude their contractual relationship after extended discussions. The agency said it would support the actor's new beginning and thanked him for helping shape the company's direction and values.
Blitzway also noted Ju's 16-year relationship with its key executives, saying their decision followed conversations about their respective futures.
MyDaily reported that Ju is taking the independent route alongside a management director who has worked with him for more than a decade. According to the outlet, he is also assembling a new team.
The actor began a new chapter with H& Entertainment in 2020. The agency was acquired and merged into Blitzway in October 2023, MyDaily reported.

Ju made his debut as a model in 2003 before beginning his acting career with the 2006 drama "Princess Hours." MyDaily reported that he is appearing in Disney+'s "The Remarried Empress" and has finished filming the Netflix original "Viking." He is also working on a new season of "The Trauma Code: Heroes on Call."

Based on Baek Young Ok’s 2012 novel of the same name, the film follows flight attendant Sa Gang, played by Suzy, and consultant Ji Hoon, played by Lee Jin Uk. At the breakfast meeting, participants share their experiences and exchange mementos connected to past relationships.

The trailer opens with Sa Gang ending a relationship before showing her and Ji Hoon at the gathering. One scene follows Sa Gang as she leaves with a Rolleiflex camera carrying traces of Ji Hoon’s previous relationship. Ji Hoon then tries to retrieve it.
Sa Gang is dealing with her breakup from airline captain Jung Soo, played by Yoo Ji Tae. Ji Hoon, meanwhile, is looking back on a long relationship with Hyun Jung, played by Keum Sae Rok.

items.dek: Nam Ji Hyun, Kim Jun Han and Jung Jae Sung appear in character to congratulate Cha Eun Kyung on the launch of law firm Rebom.
body: A new Good Partner 2 teaser has brought familiar faces from the first season together to mark a new chapter for Jang Nara's Cha Eun Kyung.

The video features messages from colleagues at Daejeong, the law firm Cha Eun Kyung previously worked for, as she launches her own firm, Rebom. Nam Ji Hyun appears as lawyer Han Yu Ri, alongside Kim Jun Han as Daejeong CEO Jung Woo Jin and Jung Jae Sung as former CEO Oh Dae Gyu.

Han Yu Ri offers her congratulations on Rebom's beginning, while Jung Woo Jin celebrates the opening. Oh Dae Gyu gives Cha Eun Kyung a more pointed endorsement, describing her as intense and stubborn but praising her ability to secure what her clients are owed.

According to Soompi, the second season follows star divorce lawyer Cha Eun Kyung as she becomes partners with Kang Hye Sung, an experienced lawyer played by Kim Hye Yoon. The two will work together on divorce cases.
Good Partner 2 premieres on November 20 at 9:50 p.m. KST and will be available on Viki.

items.headline: NCT DREAM Earns Ninth Million-Selling First Week With 'DREAM AFTER DREAM'
items.dek: The group joins SEVENTEEN as the only artists with nine albums to pass 1 million first-week sales on Hanteo.
body: NCT DREAM has reached another sales milestone with its studio album “DREAM AFTER DREAM.” The release sold 1,002,558 copies in its first week, according to Hanteo Chart figures reported by Soompi.

The total covers sales from November 9 to 15 and makes “DREAM AFTER DREAM” the group’s ninth album to sell more than 1 million copies within its first week. NCT DREAM is the second artist in Hanteo history to reach that mark with nine albums, following SEVENTEEN.

The album arrived with the upbeat title track “Boogie Woogie.” It follows eight other NCT DREAM releases that cleared the same first-week threshold: “Hot Sauce,” “Glitch Mode,” “Candy,” “ISTJ,” “DREAM( )SCAPE,” “DREAMSCAPE,” “Go Back To The Future” and “Beat It Up.”

items.headline: P1Harmony Earns First Billboard Top Album Sales No. 1 With 'BLOW UP'
items.dek: The mini album also opens at No. 4 on the Billboard 200, tying the group's previous peak with 'UNIQUE.'
body: P1Harmony has landed its first No. 1 on Billboard's Top Album Sales chart with “BLOW UP,” as the mini album becomes the best-selling album of the week in the United States.
The release also debuted at No. 4 on the Billboard 200, matching the group's highest position on the chart. P1Harmony previously reached No. 4 with “UNIQUE” in March, according to Billboard.

For the tracking week ending November 12, “BLOW UP” earned 45,000 equivalent album units in the United States, Luminate data showed. That total included 43,500 in traditional album sales and 1,500 streaming equivalent album units, representing 1.56 million on-demand official streams.

Billboard reported that the album's first-week sales were supported by 25 CD variants and five vinyl variants. The editions contained collectibles such as photocards and posters, with some items randomized.

“BLOW UP” is P1Harmony's third top 10 entry on the Billboard 200 and its seventh appearance on the chart overall, Soompi reported. Alongside “UNIQUE,” the group's earlier top 10 release was “EX,” which peaked at No. 9 in 2025.

items.headline: ILLIT's 'BREAK EVEN' tops Billboard World Albums chart as IVE debuts at No. 2
items.dek: ILLIT scored a World Albums No. 1 and a Billboard 200 milestone, while Stray Kids placed four releases on the chart.
body: ILLIT's mini album "BREAK EVEN" has reached No. 1 on Billboard's World Albums chart for the week ending November 14, following its physical release in the United States.

The release also became the group's first top 10 album on the Billboard 200 and its first No. 1 on the Top Album Sales chart, Soompi reported. ILLIT had a second entry on World Albums with "MAMIHLAPINATAPAI," which ranked No. 22 in its 27th week.
IVE followed at No. 2 with "Looks Can Kill." The mini album also marked the group's first appearance on the Billboard 200.
Stray Kids placed four albums on World Albums, led by "THIS & THAT" at No. 3. "KARMA" came in at No. 7, "DO IT" at No. 19 and "ATE" returned to the chart at No. 25.

CORTIS held two spots with "GREENGREEN" at No. 4 and debut EP "COLOR OUTSIDE THE LINES" at No. 20. ENHYPEN's "THE SIN : BLISS" remained at No. 5, while League of Legends virtual group K/DA took No. 8 with "FIRESTARTER."
BTS had three entries: "Map of the Soul: 7 ~The Journey~" at No. 10, "Love Yourself: Answer" at No. 13 and "Love Yourself: Tear" at No. 24. NMIXX's "Strange Muse" ranked No. 12 in its second week.

Other entries included BOYNEXTDOOR's "HOME" at No. 16, NewJeans' "Get Up" at No. 17, ATEEZ's "GOLDEN HOUR : Part.5" at No. 18 and LE SSERAFIM's "PUREFLOW" at No. 23. "Get Up" reached its 165th week on the chart.

items.headline: ILLIT Tops Soompi's K-Pop Chart as RESCENE Debuts at No. 2
items.dek: “You're Under Arrest” reaches No. 1 in its second chart week, while new songs by RESCENE and TWS enter the top 10.
body: ILLIT has taken the top spot on Soompi's K-pop music chart for the third week of November 2026. “You're Under Arrest” climbed one place to No. 1 in its second week on the chart.

RESCENE followed at No. 2 with “With,” which made its chart debut. The song is the title track of the group's fourth mini album, “PULSE.” Its story centers on finally meeting someone long dreamed of after following a voice calling out to them.
IVE's “Looks Can Kill” completed the top three, falling two places from No. 1. The week's other new top 10 entry came from TWS, whose “Call My Name” debuted at No. 7.
“Call My Name” is the title track of TWS's second single album, “TO US.” Its sound combines drums and bass with jazz piano played by Yun Seok Cheol.

Soompi's chart combines Korean music chart rankings with data on artists trending on the site. Circle singles and albums account for 30 percent of the calculation, followed by Hanteo singles and albums and YouTube K-pop songs and music videos at 20 percent each. Apple Music Korea and Soompi airplay each contribute 15 percent.

PLAVE presented “Watch Me Woo!,” “Star Trace” and “Born Savage.” ILLIT performed “You're Under Arrest” and “It's Me,” and KiiiKiii's set featured “Pop Off Pop Off,” “Delulu” and “404 (New Era).”

LNGSHOT brought four songs to the show: “Saucin,” “Backseat,” “Moonwalkin” and “Bananas.” CORTIS performed “MONEYMONEYMONEY,” “REDRED” and “YOUNGCREATORCREW,” while ALPHA DRIVE ONE's set included “FREAK ALARM” and “BORN DIRE.”

items.headline: BTS, IVE and CORTIS take top honors as Melon Music Awards 2026 wraps up
items.dek: BTS finished the two-night ceremony with six awards, while IVE earned five and CORTIS received its first Daesang.
body: BTS, IVE and CORTIS claimed the final three grand prizes at the Melon Music Awards 2026, which concluded November 15 at Gocheok Sky Dome in Seoul.

BTS won Artist of the Year, IVE took Song of the Year for "BANG BANG," and CORTIS received Record of the Year. Soompi reported that five Daesangs were awarded across the two nights, including BTS's Album of the Year win for "ARIRANG" and aespa's Global K-Artist of the Year award on Day 1.

BTS led the overall tally with six awards, also picking up Best Male Group, TOP10, Global TOP10 and Stage of the Year. The group was unable to attend because of its tour schedule and delivered an acceptance message by video.

IVE collected five trophies, including Best Female Group and Best Music Video for "BANG BANG," alongside TOP10 and Global TOP10 honors. During their acceptance speeches, the members thanked fans and staff, with Ahn Yujin reflecting on the work that goes into each release ahead of the group's fifth anniversary.

CORTIS finished with three awards, earning spots in both the TOP10 and Global TOP10 in addition to its first Daesang. ILLIT and KiiiKiii were recognized for Best Female Performance, while ALPHA DRIVE ONE and LNGSHOT received New Artist of the Year awards.
The 18th edition of the Melon Music Awards expanded to two days for the first time. Day 2 performers included IVE, NCT 127, NCT WISH, PLAVE, ILLIT and CORTIS.

items.dek: The NCT member plays rookie officer Ji Dae Sae in the upcoming traffic crime drama, premiering November 16.
body: NCT's Jisung is drawing attention at the police station in a new teaser for “Crash 2,” where he plays rookie officer Ji Dae Sae.

The clip begins with Min So Hee, played by Kwak Sun Young, and Eo Hyun Kyung, played by Moon Hee, hearing a commotion. When they go to see what is happening, they find Ji Dae Sae dancing for a group of fellow officers.

His performance leaves the pair wondering whether he is a celebrity. Min So Hee comments on how well his uniform suits him, while Eo Hyun Kyung thinks he looks like an idol and suspects a production may be filming at the station.

Yang Jo Ah's Yeom Bo Yeon then introduces the rookie to the two officers. When Min So Hee asks why she is so excited given that she is pregnant, Yeom Bo Yeon jokes that pregnancy does not stop her from appreciating the view.

“Crash 2” follows the 2024 drama “Crash.” In the new installment, the Traffic Crime Investigation team from Namgang Police Station becomes a regional investigative unit under the National Office of Investigation, handling traffic crime cases across the country.

items.dek: BTS collected three awards, while KATSEYE and the film KPop Demon Hunters also earned recognition.
body: BTS won three awards at the 2026 Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards, joining fellow winners Rosé, Jennie and KATSEYE. The ceremony took place on November 14, Soompi reported.

The group won every category in which it was nominated: Favorite Music Group, Favorite Song for “SWIM” and Favorite Album for “ARIRANG.” The Favorite Music Group win extended BTS's record in the category, which it previously won for four consecutive years from 2020 through 2023.

BLACKPINK members Rosé and Jennie each picked up an individual award. Rosé won Favorite Female Artist, while Jennie took Favorite Music Collaboration for “Dracula,” her collaboration with Tame Impala.
KATSEYE won Favorite Female Breakout Artist/Group and shared a brief acceptance speech. The animated film KPop Demon Hunters also had multiple wins, including Favorite Song from a Movie for “Golden.”

Two performers from the film were recognized for their voice roles. Arden Cho, who voiced Rumi, won Favorite Female Animated Voice from a Movie, while Ahn Hyo Seop, the voice of Jinu, won Favorite Male Animated Voice from a Movie.

items.headline: Yim Si Wan's Character Faces a New Truth in 'Love in Disguise'
items.dek: A secret about Seol In Ah's undercover secretary is out, but another could put her relationship with Yim Si Wan's chaebol heir at risk.
body: Yoon Yi Jun and Kang Jae Hee's relationship is heading into uncertain territory in "Love in Disguise," after an accident exposed one part of her undercover identity.

The romance thriller stars Yim Si Wan as Yi Jun, a chaebol heir suspected of murder, and Seol In Ah as Jae Hee, a former special forces officer investigating him. She has been working undercover as his personal secretary while posing as a man.

Yi Jun was initially wary of his new secretary, but his defenses began to fall as Jae Hee repeatedly put herself in danger to protect him. He eventually confessed his feelings for her, only to be rejected. Jae Hee, meanwhile, was wrestling with the fact that she was deceiving him.

A traffic accident then revealed that Jae Hee is a woman, leaving the pair to confront what that means for their relationship. Her work as an undercover detective remains a secret from Yi Jun, though he has already seen her meeting discreetly with fellow officer Kim Seok Jin, played by Nam Hae Jun.
Whether Jae Hee tells Yi Jun the truth about her investigation, or he discovers it himself, is another question facing the pair. The next episode airs November 15 at 8:50 p.m. KST, Soompi reported.

The preview shows Yeonjun making pasta inspired by Ku Sung Hwan's on-screen cooking. He also takes a cue from the actor as he cleans and exercises at home, giving viewers a glimpse of how he spends time by himself.

items.headline: Chae Soo Bin's K-Drama Roles Span Airport Romance to Royal Intrigue
items.dek: A Soompi watchlist highlights five Chae Soo Bin performances, from a robot-themed romantic comedy to a tense marriage drama.
body: Chae Soo Bin's screen roles have taken her from an airport workplace to a royal court and into some unusual romantic arrangements. A new Soompi watchlist looks at five dramas featuring the actress, with co-stars including Lee Je Hoon, Yoo Seung Ho and Yoo Yeon Seok.

In one airport-set romance, Chae plays Han Yeo Reum, an outspoken employee who catches the attention of Lee Je Hoon's Lee Soo Yeon. He is a gifted worker who keeps his colleagues at a distance while guarding a secret.

Chae also stars opposite Yoo Seung Ho in a romantic comedy about a man who believes he has acquired a robot. His attraction becomes complicated when he discovers that Chae's Jo Ji Ah is human, testing the trust between them.

For historical romance fans, Chae appears as Jo Ha Yeon alongside Kim Yoo Jung and Park Bo Gum. Kim plays Hong Ra On, a woman serving as a eunuch to Park's Crown Prince Lee Young, who is unaware of her identity. Chae's character adds another dimension to the palace story.

Another romance pairs Chae's drama writer Na Bo Bae with Kim Young Kwang's Baek Ho Rang, an heir with an artificial heart. After a lightning strike gives Bo Bae electrical powers, she discovers that she can recharge his heart without harming him. The pair enter an agreement that brings them closer.

A more tense relationship unfolds between Chae's Hong Hee Joo and Yoo Yeon Seok's Baek Sa Eon. Hee Joo, a sign language interpreter unable to speak since a childhood accident, has spent three years in a marriage of convenience with the presidential spokesperson. Her kidnapping becomes a turning point for the couple.

items.headline: RIIZE and EJAE Join 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade Lineup
items.dek: The K-pop group and singer will perform at the New York parade on November 26, alongside artists including Queen Latifah and Wyclef Jean.
body: RIIZE and EJAE are set to perform at the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City on November 26, Soompi reports.

The two acts were named in the parade lineup announced on November 13 local time. Other performers and guests include Queen Latifah, Wyclef Jean, Jimmy Fallon and The Roots, Megan Moroney, Teddy Swims, Natasha Bedingfield, JoJo and Keke Palmer. DEVO, Icona Pop, Smash Mouth and Baha Men are also among the announced names.

The parade begins at 8:30 a.m. on Thanksgiving Day. NBC will broadcast it at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones, with a simulcast on Peacock and a live broadcast on Telemundo. An encore will air on NBC at 2 p.m. ET and PT.
Savannah Guthrie, Hoda Kotb and Al Roker will host the broadcast. The 2.5-mile route ends at Macy's flagship store in Herald Square.

This year's event marks the parade's 100th edition. It began in 1924 and was not held from 1942 through 1944 during World War II. NBC says more than 11,000 volunteers and participants will take part in this year's celebration.

items.headline: Summer Vacation Episodes 5 and 6 Put a New Romance Under Pressure
items.dek: Ha Yeon and Yu Gyeom's relationship faces fresh tension as Sae Ryeong returns to the village and another family story comes into focus.
body: Episodes 5 and 6 of “Summer Vacation” bring Kim Ha Yeon and Jo Yu Gyeom together, but their new relationship is quickly complicated by the search for Seong Sae Ryeong and the fallout from her return.
Spoilers for episodes 5 and 6 follow.

After Sae Ryeong leaves, Ha Yeon, played by Cho Yi Hyun, persuades Yu Gyeom, played by Jin Young, to look for her for the sake of Sae Ryeong's grandmother. Their search takes them back to Seoul, where Sae Ryeong, played by Hong Ye Ji, meets another of Yu Gyeom's older sisters, who ran away years earlier.

Once Sae Ryeong returns to the village, her former friends bully and ostracize her. She also blames Ha Yeon for her suffering, even though Ha Yeon does not take part in the bullying. Yu Gyeom's decision to stand up for Sae Ryeong adds to the strain between him and Ha Yeon.

The episodes also spend time with Yu Gyeom's sister Jo Sam Hee, played by Shin Gi Hwan, and Ha Yeon's older brother Kim Jeong Yeon, played by Ryu Hae Jun. As the two grow closer, Jeong Yeon's troubled past and his memories of another girl complicate their connection. Sam Hee's romantic interest, meanwhile, remains one-sided.
With Sae Ryeong back in the village, Ha Yeon and Yu Gyeom must navigate the tensions surrounding her while their own relationship is still new.

items.headline: BTS's Jimin Leads November Boy Group Member Brand Reputation Ranking
items.dek: ATEEZ's San and GOT7's Park Jinyoung followed Jimin in the Korean Business Research Institute's monthly ranking.
body: BTS's Jimin held the No. 1 spot in the November brand reputation ranking for individual boy group members, according to the Korean Business Research Institute. ATEEZ's San rose to second place, while GOT7's Park Jinyoung took third.

The institute analyzed data for 755 boy group members collected from October 14 to November 14, Soompi reported. The ranking combines measures of consumer participation, media coverage, communication and community awareness.

Jimin recorded a brand reputation index of 4,733,558. Among the prominent phrases associated with him were “ARMY,” “Who” and “Jimtober.” His positivity-negativity analysis showed 95.23 percent positive reactions.
San's index rose 34.30 percent from October to 3,998,906. Park Jinyoung saw the largest month-to-month increase among the top five, with his score climbing 446.38 percent to 3,835,884.

ATEEZ's Wooyoung followed closely in fourth place with an index of 3,819,078, up 175.19 percent from the previous month. BTS's Jungkook completed the top five with 3,661,070, a 5.99 percent increase from October.

items.headline: Kim Yun Seok and Koo Kyo Hwan Face Off in New 'White Blast' Stills
items.dek: The mystery thriller follows two railway workers whose encounter with a body turns a snowbound station into a scene of mounting tension.
body: Kim Yun Seok and Koo Kyo Hwan are at odds in new stills from “White Blast,” a mystery thriller set at a rural train station cut off by heavy snow.

Kim plays Gap Soo, a stationmaster approaching retirement, while Koo plays his newly appointed successor, Hyun Taek. Their relationship becomes strained after a mysterious body is discovered at Seoloh Station.

One image shows Gap Soo pointing a rifle at Hyun Taek, who holds a shovel in defense. Another captures the men struggling over the gun, with Hyun Taek bloodied. Other stills show Gap Soo facing the storm and Hyun Taek watching his surroundings warily.
The tension extends beyond the two station workers. Detective Choi, played by Park Soo Young, and Officer Yang, played by Roh Yoon Seo, are also seen looking suspiciously at Hyun Taek.

Koo encouraged viewers to follow the story from the characters’ different perspectives, including those of Gap Soo and Hyun Taek. Director Hong Eui Jeong said she hopes audiences enjoy how their judgments change as incidents unfold, and praised the experience the two lead actors brought to their scenes together.
Kim said he hopes the film meets audiences’ expectations. “White Blast” opens in theaters on November 18.

items.headline: Crash 2 Cast Previews Nationwide Cases and NCT's Jisung's New Role
items.dek: The traffic crime drama returns with a wider investigative remit, unresolved cases and a new recruit played by NCT's Jisung.
body: The team at the center of "Crash" is taking its investigations nationwide in season 2, with NCT's Jisung joining returning stars Lee Min Ki and Kwak Sun Young. The new season premieres November 16 at 10 p.m. KST on ENA.

According to Soompi, the Traffic Crime Investigation team, known as T.C.I., moves from Namgang Police Station to a regional unit under the National Office of Investigation. The follow-up to the 2024 drama brings the team into cases across the country.

Lee Min Ki, who plays analytical investigator Cha Yeon Ho, pointed to more intricate crimes and a larger scale as highlights. He also said the season will address cases that began in the first installment and explore the team's chemistry with its newest member.

That newcomer is Ji Dae Se, a passionate young officer played by Jisung. The NCT member encouraged viewers to watch how his character contributes to the team, alongside the season's broader range of stories.

Kwak Sun Young returns as Min So Hee, who faces trauma from her past while pursuing criminals. She teased closer teamwork among the investigators and stories about new villains and their secrets. Moon Hee, who plays information gatherer Eo Hyun Kyung, also highlighted the villains and the team members' personal stories.

Heo Sung Tae reprises his role as team leader Jung Chae Man and drew attention to the evolving forms of traffic crime portrayed in the drama. Lee Ho Chul returns as Woo Dong Gi, the team's car expert and analyst, and described the series as an easy watch. The new season will also be available on Genie TV and Disney+.

items.dek: Kai and Sehun will bring their first fan concert tour, SILENT CITY, to eight locations following the release of their debut mini album.
body: EXO-KASE, the new unit featuring EXO members Kai and Sehun, has announced the dates and stops for its first fan concert tour, SILENT CITY.

The tour will open with two shows on January 9 and 10 at Korea University Hwajeong Tiger Dome in Seoul, Soompi reported. After the Seoul concerts, the duo will visit Kuala Lumpur, Macau, Jakarta, Tokyo, Bangkok, Taipei and Manila.

Seoul tickets will be sold through Melon Ticket. Members of EXO's official fan club, EXO-L, can take part in the domestic presale on November 23, followed by the global presale on November 24. General sales will open on November 25.
Before the tour begins, Kai and Sehun will release their debut mini album as EXO-KASE. Titled Waking Up The City, the album is scheduled for December 1.
EXO-KASE announced the tour dates and destinations on November 13. SILENT CITY marks the duo's first fan concert tour together as a unit.

items.headline: Jang Nara and Kim Hye Yoon team up in new Good Partner 2 teaser
items.dek: The SBS divorce drama returns on November 20 with a new legal partnership and a fresh set of difficult cases.
body: Jang Nara and Kim Hye Yoon are joining forces as divorce lawyers in Good Partner 2, which has released a new teaser ahead of its November 20 premiere.

The SBS drama brings back Jang Nara as star attorney Cha Eun Kyung, who becomes partners with experienced lawyer Kang Hye Sung, played by Kim Hye Yoon. P.O also reprises his role as Jeon Eun Ho, now a more seasoned lawyer. Park Hae Jin appears in the teaser as Park Tae Soo.

As Soompi reports, the preview begins with Eun Kyung asking a client whether they have considered divorce. It then moves through cases involving infidelity, violence and one-sided open marriages, while the lawyers weigh how to hold people accountable and listen to what their clients want.

The new season follows the lawyers as they help clients navigate choices about their lives after divorce. Writer Choi Yu Na, who is also a divorce attorney, said she wanted to offer viewers something new while retaining the familiarity that fans of the first season enjoyed.

Choi identified family and growth as key themes, with the cases exploring relationships as well as divorce. Director Seo Min Jung also said she wanted to show how people can confront their wounds and grow through understanding and relying on others.
Good Partner 2 premieres at 9:50 p.m. KST on SBS and will be available on Viki.

items.headline: 5 K-dramas to watch after Dive into You
items.dek: From a campus romance to a time-travel love story, these picks offer more of Park Seo Ham and Kim Ji Yeon or a familiar journey into the past.
body: With Dive into You now finished, fans looking for their next watch have options that follow its stars into very different stories. Soompi has highlighted five dramas featuring Park Seo Ham, Kim Ji Yeon or another romance shaped by time travel.

Semantic Error pairs Park Seo Ham with Jaechan in a campus romance. Jaechan plays computer science student Chu Sang Woo, who submits a group project under his own name after his teammates fail to contribute. Park's Jang Jae Yeong loses credit as a result and sets out to disrupt Sang Woo's orderly life.

Park also appears in Our Universe as Park Yun Seong, the first love and new boss of Woo Hyeon Jin, played by Roh Jeong Eui. The drama centers on Hyeon Jin and Seon Tae Hyeong, played by Bae In Hyuk, as the in-laws raise the child of their deceased siblings.

For more of Kim Ji Yeon, The Haunted Palace takes viewers to the Joseon Dynasty. She plays Yeo Ri, a glass artisan from a family of shamans, who faces palace spirits after her first love Yoon Gap, played by Yook Sungjae, becomes possessed.

Kim takes on a high school thriller in Pyramid Game, based on the webtoon of the same name. Her character, transfer student Sung Su Ji, challenges a popularity ranking system that makes the lowest-ranked student a target of violence.

Fans drawn to the time-travel element of Dive into You can also try Lovely Runner. Kim Hye Yoon plays Im Sol, who repeatedly travels back in time to save her favorite idol, Ryu Seon Jae, played by Byeon Woo Seok.

items.headline: Song Hye Kyo and Gong Yoo Enter the Music Industry in New Tantara Teaser
items.dek: Netflix has unveiled character posters and a teaser for the drama, which will roll out in three parts beginning December 11.
body: Song Hye Kyo and Gong Yoo chase success in Korea's entertainment industry in a new teaser for Netflix drama "Tantara," alongside Seolhyun and Cha Seung Won.
Set in the Korean entertainment world from the 1960s through the 1980s, the series follows people with little to their names as they pursue careers in an industry marked by violence and hardship.

Song plays Min Ja, while Gong takes the role of Dong Gu. The two characters have relied on each other since facing difficulties together as children. In the teaser, they meet Min Hee, a gifted singer played by Seolhyun, and enter the music industry together.

The newly released character posters offer a glimpse of what drives the cast. Min Ja sees an opportunity to make money, while Dong Gu appears undaunted by the challenges ahead. Min Hee's poster points to her complicated relationship with Min Ja and her fear of being abandoned.
Cha plays Seok Gil Yeo, a star composer whose poster hints at the difficult path he took to reach his position.

"Tantara" was written by Noh Hee Kyung and directed by Lee Yoon Jung. Netflix will release the 22-episode series in three parts: episodes 1 through 8 arrive December 11, episodes 9 through 15 follow December 18, and episodes 16 through 22 land December 25.

body: NCT's Jisung is ready to learn on the job in a new first episode preview for "Crash 2," though his enthusiasm quickly catches his colleagues off guard.

The preview introduces Jisung as Ji Dae Sae, who promises to observe quietly as he joins the traffic crime investigation team. His resolve is tested when Woo Dong Gi, played by Lee Ho Chul, warns him to watch without listening. Ji Dae Sae laughs, only for Woo Dong Gi to respond sternly.

Later, as Min So Hee and Cha Yeon Ho, played by Kwak Sun Young and Lee Min Ki, discuss a case, Ji Dae Sae excitedly asks whether it involves a judge's daughter who claims her car suddenly accelerated. His interruption surprises the team, prompting Woo Dong Gi to question why he spoke.

The sequel to the 2024 drama "Crash" follows the Traffic Crime Investigation team as it moves beyond Namgang Police Station. Now a regional investigative unit under the National Office of Investigation, the team takes on traffic crime cases across the country.

body: SBS has released a new teaser for “Nine to Six,” offering a glimpse of Park Min Young's character as she navigates a demanding job and the attention of two men at work.

Park stars as a workaholic who has put romance aside to focus on her career. BTOB's Yook Sungjae plays Han Seon Woo, a warm and thoughtful colleague who helps her open up to love as they grow together in their personal and professional lives.

The teaser finds Park's character having a difficult day after being reprimanded for sticking closely to the rules at work. Seon Woo tries to lift her spirits, offering her a chance to have fun with him.
She also catches the attention of Park Hyun Tae, a new division head played by Go Soo. He tells her that he finds himself doing things he had not planned when they are together.
The two men's interest leads to a tense exchange. Seon Woo asks Hyun Tae directly whether he likes her, while Hyun Tae questions why Seon Woo is going so far.

As Park's character grows closer to Seon Woo, she reflects that spending time with him makes her feel like a better person. The teaser closes with an exchange about doing everything together, prompting her to ask whether he means for a lifetime.
“Nine to Six” premieres on November 25 at 9 p.m. KST.

body: Happy Anding kept its lead over What a Boss Wants as the two dramas aired their second episodes on November 12.

According to Nielsen Korea figures reported by Soompi, tvN's Happy Anding recorded an average nationwide rating of 1.7 percent, unchanged from its premiere the night before. MBN's What a Boss Wants posted 1.0 percent nationwide, dipping slightly from its first episode.

Happy Anding follows three comedians who have spent a decade struggling to establish themselves. Kang Hoon plays Kang Tae Gu, alongside Cho Hyun Chul as Kim Nam Il and Kim Jung Jin as Han Jun Seo. Their search for new directions begins after they encounter a mysterious woman.

What a Boss Wants takes a romantic approach, with Sung Hoon playing Kwon Do Hyuk, a chaebol boss searching for a woman whose voice he heard on an album. Oh Se Young stars as Lee Eun Chae, an indie band's lead vocalist who becomes an unexpected presence in his carefully ordered life.

items.headline: CL signs with THEBLACKLABEL, plans November song release
items.dek: The 2NE1 member is joining producer Teddy's agency after years of working together, with a new song in preparation.
body: CL has signed an exclusive contract with THEBLACKLABEL and is aiming to release a new song in November, the agency announced on November 13.

The move brings the 2NE1 member together again with Teddy, THEBLACKLABEL's founder and a longtime musical collaborator. The agency said their new partnership is built on trust developed over years of working together, and that CL is preparing to meet fans around the world.
CL debuted as 2NE1's leader under YG Entertainment in 2009. Teddy participated in the production of several of the group's best-known songs, including “FIRE,” “I DON'T CARE” and “I AM THE BEST.”
After leaving YG in 2019, CL established her own agency, Very Cherry, and continued her solo career independently. She released her first full-length solo album, “ALPHA,” in 2021.
At THEBLACKLABEL, CL joins a roster that includes fellow former YG artists Taeyang of BIGBANG and Rosé of BLACKPINK. Jeon Somi, MEOVV and ALLDAY PROJECT are also among the agency's artists.

The signing marks a new chapter for CL alongside a producer who helped shape some of 2NE1's most recognizable releases. Her planned November song will follow the announcement of her exclusive contract.

items.headline: Five Ryan Cheng dramas to watch, from The Lament of Autumn to My Journey to You
items.dek: The actor, also known as Cheng Lei, takes on commanders, a prince and a fictional villain in five dramas highlighted by Soompi.
body: Ryan Cheng has played characters driven by ambition, loyalty and revenge across historical dramas and fantasy romances. A Soompi roundup highlights five roles that show different sides of the actor, from a ruthless commander to a villain who crosses from fiction into the real world.

In The Lament of Autumn, Cheng plays Yu Chang Xuan, commander-in-chief of the Yu army's Nine Corps. His pursuit of student Ye Ping Jun, played by Xu Ruo Han, becomes increasingly obsessive despite her clear dislike of him.

Legend of the Female General casts Cheng as Xiao Jue, a disciplined military leader seeking justice for his family. He grows close to He Yan, played by Zhou Ye, after she joins his camp disguised as a male recruit.

In The First Jasmine, Cheng's Prince Mo Xiu Yao is a former war hero whose marriage to Ye Li, played by Bai Lu, begins as a reluctant alliance. As they live together, both pursue plans to avenge past wrongs.

My Journey to You sees Cheng play Gong Shang Jue, a strategist protective of the Gong family. His suspicion of his cousin Gong Zi Yu, played by Zhang Ling He, adds to a power struggle complicated by the arrival of people with hidden identities.

For a change of setting, The Killers Is Also Romantic places Cheng's fictional antagonist Lu Zi Ye alongside novelist Hua Qing Ge, played by Song Yi Ren. After entering the real world, Lu Zi Ye becomes involved in a murder case that leads him and Hua Qing Ge to investigate together.

items.headline: NCT's Jisung Joins Returning Cast in New 'Crash 2' Set Photos
items.dek: The rookie officer joins Lee Min Ki and the returning traffic crime investigation team as the drama prepares for its November 16 premiere.
body: NCT's Jisung is joining the investigation in “Crash 2,” with newly released behind-the-scenes photos offering a look at him alongside the drama's returning cast.

The second season follows the Traffic Crime Investigation team as it moves from Namgang Police Station to a regional unit under the National Office of Investigation. The team will take on traffic crime cases across the country.

Lee Min Ki returns as T.C.I. ace Cha Yeon Ho, while Kwak Sun Young reprises her role as Min So Hee and Heo Sung Tae plays team leader Jung Chae Man. In the new photos, Lee is focused on filming, Kwak smiles on set and Heo reviews his script.

Lee Ho Chul is also back as traffic crime analyst Woo Dong Gi, alongside Moon Hee as Eo Hyun Kyung, whose skills include gathering information and martial arts. Jisung joins them as rookie police officer Ji Dae Se.

The returning actors said they quickly settled back into working together after two years. Lee Min Ki recalled that the cast felt familiar with one another at the first shoot, while Kwak Sun Young and Heo Sung Tae described the reunion as comfortable.
Jisung said the actors and staff helped him feel at ease on set. He added that he learned a lot from working with the senior actors.
“Crash 2” premieres November 16 at 10 p.m. KST on ENA. It will also be available on Genie TV and Disney+.

items.headline: Lee Dong Wook Reviewing Offer for Historical Action Film Nambeol
items.dek: The actor is in talks for a role previously offered to Seo Kang Jun in a Joseon-era film starring Lee Byung Hun.
body: Lee Dong Wook is reviewing an offer to appear in the upcoming historical action film Nambeol, according to its production company, Hive Media Corp.

The role was previously offered to Seo Kang Jun, whose decision to turn it down was confirmed a day earlier. MyDaily reported on November 12 that Lee Dong Wook would play the right-hand man of Lee Byung Hun's character. Hive Media Corp said the actor was still considering the offer, Soompi reported.

Set in the early Joseon dynasty, Nambeol, a literal title, follows nine warriors from different social ranks as they travel to Tsushima Island. Their mission is to rescue captives abducted by Japanese pirates. The film combines martial arts and action in a hard-boiled story.

The previously confirmed cast includes Lee Byung Hun, Go Youn Jung, Lee Do Hyun, WOODZ, also known as Cho Seung Youn, Park Hae Joon and Lee Kwang Soo. MyDaily reported that the part offered to Lee Dong Wook is one of the nine warriors.
Nambeol would mark another collaboration between Lee Dong Wook and Hive Media Corp. The actor previously worked with the production company on the films A Year-End Medley and Harbin.

items.headline: Oh Se Young and Sung Hoon Begin a Rocky Office Partnership in What a Boss Wants
items.dek: New stills preview Lee Eun Chae's first day as Kwon Do Hyuk's assistant, complete with a tense assignment and an accidental embrace.
body: Oh Se Young and Sung Hoon are taking their bickering to the workplace in the second episode of “What a Boss Wants.” New stills show their characters starting a complicated boss and assistant relationship, Soompi reports.

Based on a web novel, the romance drama stars Sung Hoon as Kwon Do Hyuk, a chaebol boss with no sense of taste who is searching for a woman whose voice he heard on an album. Oh Se Young plays Lee Eun Chae, the lead vocalist of indie band India Red.

Do Hyuk previously spotted someone called Soo on an India Red CD cover who looked identical to an AI singer he had created. He went to the band's performance venue to find her, but Eun Chae concealed her identity. Her suspicious behavior and a red dress in her bag later convinced him that she was Soo.

The new stills show Eun Chae arriving for her first day at Do Hyuk's office as his executive assistant. She stands her ground against his demanding requests, while her commitment to performing with India Red adds another complication. According to Xports News, she tries to leave work using an English class as an excuse, only for Do Hyuk to order her back.

Another scene brings them unexpectedly close. Eun Chae presses her ear against the door of Do Hyuk's laboratory, but the door opens and she falls into his arms. The pair are visibly embarrassed, and Do Hyuk also ends up speaking with her father by phone.
Episode 2 airs November 12 at 10:20 p.m. KST.

items.headline: ATEEZ Look Ahead With 'UP' After 'BAD' Success
items.dek: The group discussed their 15th mini album, music video highlights and hopes for future performances at a comeback press conference.
body: ATEEZ are preparing to return with their 15th mini album, “GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6,” and title track “UP,” following the success of “BAD.” At a press conference ahead of the release, the members reflected on their progress and shared what fans can look forward to.

According to Soompi, leader Hongjoong said the comeback carries a message that ATEEZ are still moving forward eight years into their career. He also described the release as meaningful in connection with the group’s eighth anniversary.

The members pointed to several moments in the “UP” music video and performance. Hongjoong highlighted a final scene in which San breaks through a wall, while Wooyoung drew attention to Seonghwa’s dance break. Yeosang said he felt some pressure taking on a standout dance moment after San’s performance in “BAD,” but added that every member has a moment to watch in “UP.”

Jongho singled out “Hollow Victory” as a B-side to anticipate. Meanwhile, the members recalled a break during the video shoot when Yunho and Yeosang discovered a soy-marinated crab restaurant, then brought the rest of the group along. Yunho said they ate there two days in a row.

Looking beyond the comeback, Seonghwa said the group hopes to deliver strong performances at upcoming events, including awards shows. Yunho credited fans, known as ATINY, as a driving force behind the group’s eight years of promotions, while Hongjoong expressed excitement for an upcoming tour.
“GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6” and “UP” are set for release on November 13 at 2 p.m. KST.

body: Han Hyo Joo and Gong Myoung are bringing a high school first love story to the baseball field in MBC's upcoming drama "Your Ground." New stills show their characters together years after they first met, with a professional partnership now connecting them.

Han plays Seo Hee Seung, a former star lawyer at a major firm who has chosen a new career as a professional baseball agent. Gong plays Kang Hae Hwan, a right-handed pitcher for the Miracles who once reached Major League Baseball. After an unexpected incident, he has spent two years in rehabilitation.

The pair met 11 years earlier at Ilseong High School, where Hee Seung was the top student and Hae Hwan was the baseball team's star. They were each other's first loves, and their reunion comes as Hee Seung works to help Hae Hwan return to his career.

In one of the newly released images, they sit side by side in the stands at a baseball stadium. Hae Hwan looks ahead while Hee Seung smiles with her arms crossed. Other stills show them in a flower-filled space and on a tree-lined path, where they hold hands.
"Your Ground" is scheduled to premiere in December as an MBC Friday-Saturday drama. Lee Sang Yeob and Kang Chae Won direct the series, with Hwang Hae Yeon writing the script.

items.headline: Stray Kids' Lee Know Prepares for Solo Debut in Early 2027
items.dek: JYP Entertainment has confirmed that Lee Know is working on a solo album, with an early 2027 release as the goal.
body: Stray Kids member Lee Know is preparing to make his official solo debut, with JYP Entertainment targeting an early 2027 release for his first solo album.

A JYP representative confirmed the plans to Dispatch, Soompi reported on November 12. Dispatch reported that the album is expected in January, although the agency described the timing more broadly as early 2027.

Earlier on November 12, Newsen reported that Lee Know had completed the album jacket shoot and filmed portions of a music video in October. The outlet said he was in the final stages of preparation for the album.
The release would make Lee Know the first Stray Kids member to make an official solo debut. He debuted with the group in March 2018 with “District 9.”
Lee Know is also expected to begin his mandatory military service in the first quarter of 2027, according to Soompi.

The solo plans follow a busy period for Stray Kids. The group's August mini album “THIS & THAT” earned its ninth No. 1 on the Billboard 200, while the members also performed at festivals including Governors Ball and Rock in Rio.

items.headline: Kim Woo Bin Sizes Up Two Pitchers in New Poster for Baseball Drama 'GIFT'
items.dek: The tvN drama's latest poster puts Cha Been's hardworking pitcher and Han Si Hyun's natural talent on either side of Kim Woo Bin's coach.
body: Kim Woo Bin is heading to the baseball mound in a new poster for tvN's upcoming drama "GIFT," where his character has a unique way of assessing players.

Based on a webtoon, the sports drama stars Kim as Jung Min Yong, a former professional baseball pitching coach who gains a special ability after an unexpected accident. He goes on to coach a high school team ranked last in the nation.

In the poster, Jung stands with his arms crossed between pitchers Heo Seung Il, played by Cha Been, and Cha Tae Hoon, played by Han Si Hyun. The two face opposite directions as they prepare to pitch, with letters above their heads indicating the talent grades only their coach can see.
Seung Il has a C grade and works relentlessly to make up for his lack of natural talent. Tae Hoon, meanwhile, has an S grade and exceptional instincts, even though he knows little about baseball.
The contrast sets up a question at the heart of the poster: whether natural ability or hard work will make the difference when the players take the field.
"GIFT" premieres December 5 at 9:10 p.m. KST on tvN.

Jang Nara returns as Cha Eun Kyung, a star divorce lawyer, while Kim Hye Yoon plays Kang Hye Sung, an experienced lawyer committed to her clients. The two first meet as opposing counsel, representing different firms in the same suit.

In the newly released images, the lawyers confront each other in court. Other stills show a warmer side of their relationship, with the pair smiling at one another. Their path from conflict to trust will be a focus of the new season, as they navigate different personalities and approaches to work.

Jang Nara described their dynamic in terms of experience and passion. She said Kang Hye Sung reminded her of a younger Cha Eun Kyung, adding that it was fun to play characters who seemed both different and alike.
Kim Hye Yoon encouraged viewers to watch how the two lawyers support each other and grow together. P.O also returns as Jeon Eun Ho, now a more seasoned lawyer.

body: Two new Korean dramas entered the ratings race on November 11, with tvN's "Happy Anding" opening at 1.7 percent and MBN's "What a Boss Wants" recording 1.3 percent nationwide, according to Nielsen Korea figures reported by Soompi.

"What a Boss Wants" stars Sung Hoon as Kwon Do Hyuk, a chaebol boss searching for a woman whose voice he heard on an album. Oh Se Young plays Lee Eun Chae, the lead singer of an indie band whose path repeatedly crosses his.

In the premiere, Do Hyuk and Eun Chae first meet in a medical office, where she ends up pretending to be a doctor. They encounter each other again at a job interview, before Do Hyuk discovers the band and sees its vocalist performing at a club. The singer, known as Su, is Eun Chae.

Over on tvN, "Happy Anding" follows three comedians who have spent a decade trying to build their careers. Kang Hoon, Cho Hyun Chul and Kim Jung Jin play Kang Tae Gu, Kim Nam Il and Han Jun Seo, respectively.

The first episode traces the friends' journey from a high school performance to their years as the comedy trio Asura. A new producer offers them a chance to develop a comedy segment, while a mysterious woman keeps an eye on the group. She is revealed to be Go Eun Young, a worker at their regular cafe, played by Lee Yi Dam.

items.headline: IVE and RIIZE Lead Circle Weekly Charts as A2O LITE Keeps Triple Crown
items.dek: IVE topped the album chart, RIIZE led downloads and A2O LITE held three No. 1 spots for the week of October 18 to 24.
body: IVE, RIIZE and A2O LITE claimed top spots on Circle Chart’s weekly rankings for October 18 to 24, while ILLIT led the social chart and landed in the top three on several music charts.

IVE’s EP “Looks Can Kill” debuted at No. 1 on the physical album chart, followed by ILLIT’s “BREAK EVEN” at No. 2. AND2BLE’s “Sequence 02: Attraction” took the next two places, with its regular edition at No. 3 and POCA version at No. 4. XLOV’s “i=!” completed the top five.

On the digital download chart, RIIZE’s new single “Insomnia” debuted at No. 1. IVE’s “Looks Can Kill” moved to No. 2 after leading the previous week, while ILLIT’s “You’re Under Arrest” and AND2BLE’s “French Kissing” entered at Nos. 3 and 4, respectively. A2O LITE’s “NEON” placed fifth.

A2O LITE maintained a triple crown with “NEON,” which led the overall digital, streaming and global K-pop charts. It marked the song’s third consecutive week at No. 1 on both the overall digital and global K-pop rankings.

MEOMURU’s “The Adult I Dreamed Of” and i-dle member Soyeon’s “I’m gonna TOESA” followed “NEON” on the overall digital chart. On the global K-pop chart, HUNTR/X’s “Golden” returned to No. 2, ahead of ILLIT’s “You’re Under Arrest” and BTS’s “SWIM.”
ILLIT rose to No. 1 on the social chart, followed by BTS, A2O LITE, PSY and BABYMONSTER.

Their itinerary comes with one shared rule: everyone is free to choose how to spend the day, but the group must reunite for dinner. The arrangement creates smaller outings, including a workout with Park Jung Soo and Joohoney and a breakfast with Lee Seo Jin, Kim Yong Gun and Jeongyeon.

Park Jung Soo keeps busy on outings to an art museum with Lee Seo Jin and a shopping trip with Jeongyeon. Meanwhile, the two youngest cast members help with navigation and driving. Joohoney approaches Lee Seo Jin playfully, while Jeongyeon responds with delight to compliments from Park Jung Soo.

items.headline: Ahn Bo Hyun Leads an Uneasy Escort Team in New Sacred Jewel Stills
items.dek: The upcoming JTBC historical drama follows a group of warriors sent to recover a sacred relic as Goryeo faces defeat.
body: New stills from JTBC's upcoming drama "Sacred Jewel" introduce Ahn Bo Hyun and the warriors joining his character on a mission to recover a relic believed to protect their kingdom.

Set in 1258, the drama takes place as Goryeo stands close to defeat after 30 years of war with Mongolia. The story follows an expedition searching for the Avalokitesvara Bead and a princess who sets out to save its members.

Ahn plays Baek Gyeol, a former member of the elite Gyeollyonggun who is ordered to lead the escort team. His assignment requires him to work with warriors from Yabyeolcho, a group he once despised, including their leader Choi Gu, played by Lee Sung Min.

Ha Yun Kyung plays Geol Seung, the team's only female member and its guide. A former tavern owner from Ganghwa Island's market district, she joins the journey at Baek Gyeol's request. Hyun Bong Sik plays Mu Saeng, a powerful senior soldier and trusted associate of Choi Gu, while Kim Do Hyun plays Jap Son, an outspoken archer with a hunter's background.

The team also includes two assassins with contrasting personalities: Han Dam, played by Son Woo Hyun, is a formidable close-quarters fighter who lost family members in the war, while Bae Jung Nam's Ado Eul Chi is friendly and optimistic.

Ryu Yeon Seok, Ahn Do Gyu, Han Sang Jo and Gi Yoon round out the escort as Song Mu Jin, Hong Bong Yi, Sam Do and Beop Hang. Their characters include a cook, a shield-bearer who handles carrier pigeons, and a monk.
"Sacred Jewel," written by Jung Hyun Min and directed by Jung Dae Yoon, premieres December 5 at 10:40 p.m. KST.

items.headline: aespa's Karina Shares Message After Criticism of Friend Han Su-a
items.dek: Karina told fans she hoped no one would be hurt after actress Han Su-a faced hostile comments over a YouTube appearance about their friendship.
body: aespa's Karina has shared a message about the people close to her after actress Han Su-a received hostile comments for discussing their friendship on a YouTube show.

In a November 11 post on fan communication platform Bubble, Karina said she had considered whether to speak up. She described MYs, aespa's members, her family and friends as precious to her, and said she hoped no one would be hurt.

Karina added that she felt she received as much love as she gave and hoped no one would become a target. She did not name Han in the reported message, which came after criticism of the actress's appearance.

Han had spoken about Karina on the November 10 episode of Letters Between Us 2, where she wrote a letter to her friend. She recalled a time when Karina comforted her as she cried and thanked the singer for helping her through difficult moments, according to TopStarNews.

The actress said the pair met through ITZY's Ryujin and grew close over roughly a year, often spending time together. She also said she had previously been careful about mentioning Karina publicly, but asked her permission before appearing on the letter-writing show. Han said Karina agreed and chose photos for the episode.

After the video appeared, some commenters accused Han of using the singer's name for attention. Money Today reported that hostile messages appeared on Han's Instagram, including calls for her to stop mentioning Karina. Hankook Ilbo also reported that others considered the criticism an excessive intrusion into the friends' private relationship.
Karina's Bubble message closed with an affectionate note to fans, expressing her wish that they continue to see one another and share their stories for a long time.

body: Han Hyo Joo and Gong Myoung have joined their Your Ground co-stars for a script reading ahead of the baseball romance's planned December premiere on MBC, Soompi reported.

Gong Myoung plays Kang Hae Hwan, a right-handed pitcher for the Miracles whose career stalls after a setback. Han plays Seo Hee Seung, a former law firm ace who enters the world of professional baseball as an agent. The two characters were each other's first loves and reunite after 11 years.

Hee Seung leaves behind an offer to become the youngest team leader at her firm to take on her new career. Hae Hwan, once celebrated as a future ace, faces the challenge of returning to the field while carrying the emotional weight of his setback.

Sung Joon plays fellow Miracles pitcher Yoon Yi Seok, a rival who has never beaten Hae Hwan but becomes the team's ace after he leaves the mound. Kim Shin Rock plays influential agent Dong Chi Young, who negotiates between clubs and players and works toward Hae Hwan's return.

Director Lee Sang Yeob, whose previous work includes the Yumi's Cells series and My Youth, attended the reading alongside cast members Jo Han Chul, Hong Woo Jin, Kim Joong Gi, Kim Young Sung, Jo Eun Sol and Jung Soon Won. Your Ground is written by Hwang Hae Yeon.

Set in 1258, the drama takes place after 30 years of war with Mongolia have left Goryeo on the verge of defeat. An expedition heads onto the battlefield to find the Avalokitesvara Bead, a sacred relic believed to have the power to protect the nation. A princess also sets out to save the expedition.

Ahn plays Baek Gyeol, a young commander in the royal guard unit charged with protecting the emperor. In the teaser, he receives an order to lead the team searching for the bead, but the mission requires him to work with Yabyeolcho, a special military unit he has long despised.
That resentment quickly comes to the surface when Baek Gyeol meets Choi Gu, played by Lee Sung Min. The Yabyeolcho's top warrior mocks the royal guards, prompting Baek Gyeol to challenge him.
Despite their clash, Choi Gu later asks Baek Gyeol to put their differences aside and stand with his unit. Their uneasy partnership forms part of the expedition's fight to secure the relic.

items.headline: ILLIT Scores First Billboard 200 Top 10 With 'BREAK EVEN'
items.dek: The mini album also gives ILLIT its first No. 1 on Billboard's Top Album Sales chart.
body: ILLIT has earned its first top 10 entry on the Billboard 200 with “BREAK EVEN,” which debuted at No. 6 on the U.S. albums chart dated November 14.
The mini album also opened at No. 1 on Top Album Sales, making it ILLIT's first release to lead the sales chart, Soompi reported. Billboard announced the chart results on November 8.

According to Luminate, “BREAK EVEN” earned 37,000 equivalent album units in the United States during the tracking week ending November 5. That total included 32,500 traditional album sales, the group's biggest U.S. sales week yet, and 4,500 streaming equivalent units, representing 4.87 million on-demand audio streams.

The Billboard 200 ranks albums by overall consumption, including sales and streaming, while Top Album Sales focuses on traditional album purchases. “BREAK EVEN” was the week's best-selling album in the United States.

The release is ILLIT's fifth entry on the Billboard 200. Their previous albums on the chart were “SUPER REAL ME,” which peaked at No. 93, “I'LL LIKE YOU” at No. 94, “bomb” at No. 171 and “MAMIHLAPINATAPAI” at No. 26.

body: RESCENE has set a new personal sales record with its fourth mini album, “PULSE,” which sold 602,688 copies in its first week, according to Hanteo Chart.

The total covers sales from November 3 through November 9 and marks the group's first album to pass half a million sales. Soompi reported that the figure is nearly six times RESCENE's previous first-week record of 104,406 copies, set by its third mini album, “lip bomb.”
“PULSE” surpassed that earlier benchmark on its first day alone, selling 131,893 copies. By the end of the week, it had become RESCENE's best-selling album to date.
The release also brought chart success for its title track, “With.” The song reached No. 1 on Melon's Top 100, as well as the real-time charts for Bugs and Genie Music.

RESCENE debuted in 2024 and drew attention the following spring through the “Geoje Yaho” meme. The group's song “LOVE ATTACK” subsequently climbed the charts, while its remake of “Pretty Girl,” released in August, earned a music show win.

items.headline: Viki adds 16 K-dramas for streaming in Southeast Asia

body: Viki has added 16 K-dramas for viewers in Southeast Asia, according to Soompi. The selection spans supernatural mysteries, workplace stories and romance, with titles including "He Is Psychometric," "Strangers from Hell" and "Doom at Your Service."

In "He Is Psychometric," Park Jin Young plays Lee Ahn, a man who can uncover secrets through touch. His connection with Yoon Jae In, played by Shin Ye Eun, grows as she guards a painful past. "Memorist" also pairs supernatural abilities with crime-solving, following a detective played by Yoo Seung Ho and a profiler played by Lee Se Young as they pursue a serial killer.

For thriller fans, "Strangers from Hell" stars Yim Si Wan as an aspiring writer who moves into a sharehouse with unsettling residents, including a dentist played by Lee Dong Wook. "Kill It" follows a veterinarian and assassin played by Jang Ki Yong, whose dangerous life intersects with a detective played by Nana.

The romance options include "Doom at Your Service," starring Park Bo Young as a web novel editor who encounters Seo In Guk's Myul Mang after learning she has 100 days to live. In "Love Your Enemy," Ju Ji Hoon and Jung Yu Mi play former classmates with the same name and feuding families who reunite after 18 years. Sooyoung and Gong Myoung star in "Second Shot at Love," about a woman who decides to quit drinking after reconnecting with her first love.

The lineup also includes the legal dramas "Law and The City," "Military Prosecutor Doberman" and "Confession," as well as "The Queen Who Crowns," "The Killer's Shopping List," "Way Back Love," "Search," "Search: WWW" and "Save Me 2."

items.headline: Starship Pursues Legal Action Over Malicious Posts Targeting IVE's Jang Won Young
items.dek: The agency says it is reviewing evidence from fans and online monitoring as it pursues civil and criminal measures.
body: Starship Entertainment says it is pursuing legal action over malicious online activity targeting IVE member Jang Won Young. In a statement issued November 10, the agency said its response covers alleged false information, defamation, sexual harassment, personal attacks, insults and invasions of privacy.

According to Soompi, Starship is working with law firm LIWU to review evidence gathered through fan reports and the agency's own monitoring. LIWU previously represented the agency in its lawsuit against the cyberbullying channel Sojang.

Starship said it had secured evidence of suspected violations across Korean and international platforms, including YouTube, X, Instagram, TikTok, Weibo and several online communities. The agency named two YouTube channels, IVE_NO_LIVE and Dol Jal Al, among the accounts involved and said it was taking legal steps on a case-by-case basis.

The agency said collected evidence could still be used in legal proceedings if posts are deleted or accounts are made private, renamed or deactivated. It also said it would pursue available civil and criminal measures against confirmed violations without leniency.

Fans can submit reports and evidence to starship.protect@gmail.com. Starship said reporters' personal information and submitted materials would be handled securely and used only as necessary for legal proceedings.

items.headline: K-Pop’s Big Four Establish FANOMENON Company Ahead of 2027 Festival
items.dek: HYBE, SM, JYP and YG have joined forces on a company for the K-culture event planned across Seoul and Goyang in December 2027.
body: HYBE, SM Entertainment, JYP Entertainment and YG Entertainment have established a joint venture for FANOMENON, bringing four of K-pop’s largest agencies together ahead of the planned December 2027 festival.

FANOMENON Co., Ltd. was registered on October 26, 2026, according to corporate registry information reported by The Korea Herald. The company will oversee the event’s planning, production and operation, marking a step forward for a project the agencies began preparing earlier this year.

The inaugural FANOMENON is scheduled for December 2–12, 2027, at Seoul Arena in Seoul and KINTEX in Goyang, Gyeonggi Province. According to Korea.net, the plan combines K-pop concerts and fandom awards with exhibitions and interactive programs from Korean culture companies.

At Seoul Arena, the awards are envisioned as a mix of performances and honors for fan communities, with artists accepting awards on their fans’ behalf. KINTEX is planned to host multi-artist performances alongside exhibitions and hands-on experiences.

The Korea Herald reports that FANOMENON Co. launched with 4 billion won in paid-in capital. Park Yun-suh, who previously worked at HYBE and JYP, will serve as CEO, while each of the four participating agencies has a non-executive director on the board.

The company’s stated business scope extends beyond staging performances to areas including ticket sales, venue operating rights, merchandise and intellectual-property licensing. Its formation follows an April announcement by the agencies that they were preparing a collaborative company to advance the event.

The FANOMENON name combines “fan” and “phenomenon.” The project has also drawn scrutiny over its trademark, which JYP initially filed. The Korea Herald reports that a revised agreement submitted to the National Assembly divides the rights equally between the Culture Ministry and the joint venture.

“SEVENTEEN TV” brings the group into a trainee-style dorm for a two-part series made as part of promotions for their 10th-anniversary album, HAPPY BURSTDAY. The members play exaggerated characters as they reenact trainee life.

In “MC BOO’s Dangerous Invitation,” Seungkwan interviews DK while the other members face a watery penalty whenever DK says an assigned forbidden word. Once he catches on, DK starts repeating the trigger words.

“WATER BATTLEGROUNDS” sends the members into a water-gun survival game, while “Mafiapoly” combines mafia and Monopoly with three members absent. Viewers sensitive to first-person camera footage may want to take care with “WATER BATTLEGROUNDS.”

body: Bleecker Street's event cinema division Crosswalk and Universal Pictures Content Group have picked up 'Twice: This Is For… You,' the concert film built around TWICE's night at London's O2 Arena. Crosswalk takes North American rights, while Universal handles the film internationally.

The film pairs concert footage from the 'This Is For' world tour with behind-the-scenes access and new interviews with the nine members, and it is set for a worldwide theatrical release on February 5, 2027, including IMAX screenings.

Paul Dugdale and Hannah Lux Davis directed the film, which was produced by Live Nation Studios. Crosswalk will release it in the United States and Canada, with Universal Pictures International handling cinemas in other territories.

The deal continues a partnership that already delivered 'Stray Kids: The dominATE Experience' earlier this year. The 'This Is For' tour itself was one of TWICE's biggest, running 44 cities and 81 shows from its July 2025 opening at Incheon Inspire Arena to its finale at Seoul's KSPO Dome in July 2026.
It is a separate project from 'Twice: One In A Million,' the documentary marking the group's 10th anniversary that was announced during the tour's opening shows.

items.headline: K-Pop Trade Organization Responds Amid NewJeans Contract Controversy
items.dek: The Korea Popmusic Industry Association has answered the New York Times' report on NewJeans' contracts, calling it one-sided and biased.
body: The Korea Popmusic Industry Association has answered the New York Times' report on NewJeans' contracts, calling the coverage a one-sided and biased assessment in a statement of more than 800 words issued on November 9.

The Times reported on November 5 that it had obtained the exclusive contracts the five members signed with ADOR in 2022, when they were aged 14 to 17. The paper said the deals left out protections for minors' education, health, sleep and rest that appear in the government's standard contract, and included limits on relationships and criticism of the company, steep exit penalties, and rights to keep using the members' names, likenesses and AI-generated voices after the contracts end in 2029.

The association, whose members include HYBE, SM, JYP and YG, argued that the report judged the deals by individual clauses alone, without weighing supplementary agreements, Korean law, or how the contracts were actually carried out. It pointed to the government's standard contract for popular culture artists and the Popular Culture and Arts Industry Development Act as the framework that protects both companies and artists.

It also said major companies sign the government's standard supplementary agreement for minors with every trainee, covering sleep, education and rest, and appoint youth protection officers. The group described the trainee system as a distinctive model that should not be judged through a Western lens, and raised concern that contract terms under confidentiality obligations were disclosed to foreign media while legal proceedings are still ongoing.
items.socialCaption: The K-pop industry's trade body has fired back at the NYT's NewJeans contract report, calling it a one-sided take on how the industry works.
items.seoDescription: KPIA has responded to the New York Times' report on NewJeans' ADOR contracts, defending the deals as lawful and the K-pop training system as a model in its own right.

items.headline: ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ Directors Join Animated Short ‘Living With a Visionary’
items.dek: Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans have joined Stephen P. Neary's animated documentary short as executive producers, ahead of its premiere through The New York Times Op-Docs.
body: Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans, the directors behind KPop Demon Hunters, have joined the animated documentary short Living With a Visionary as executive producers. The short, narrated by James Cromwell, premieres through The New York Times Op-Docs this week.

Written, directed and animated by Stephen P. Neary, the film adapts a memoir by poet John Matthias. It follows his decades-long marriage to art curator Diana Matthias and how their life together shifts after her Parkinson's diagnosis, including the vivid hallucinations brought on by her medication, which John, now her caregiver, learns to live with alongside her.

Neary made the film with producer Mireia Vilanova, drawing thousands of illustrations by hand on layered vellum over three years, working on it during evenings and weekends around a full-time job and a teaching post at the California Institute of the Arts. The short has already picked up the grand jury prize for animation at AFI Fest and the short film jury award for animation at Sundance earlier this year.

Neary previously created and ran The Fungies! for Cartoon Network and HBO Max, supervised production on the Annie-nominated Clarence, and worked as a story artist on KPop Demon Hunters, The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs, Rio and The Peanuts Movie. Kang and Appelhans said they were drawn to the project despite how different it looks from their own film, and Neary said the two projects share the same concerns underneath. Living With a Visionary is one of nine titles on Op-Docs' 2026 slate being talked about as awards contenders.

items.headline: Korean Organizations Reject Claim of Oppressive Control in K-Pop
items.dek: Korea's music industry association says the K-pop system is dedicated management and investment, not oppressive control.
body: A leading Korean music industry body has pushed back on the idea that K-pop runs on oppressive control, after a New York Times report on NewJeans' contracts put the industry's training system under the spotlight. The Korea Popmusic Industry Association said the description dismisses a system built on dedicated management and upfront investment.

In a statement on November 9, the association argued that the Times report, which said the 2022 ADOR contracts omitted youth protections and kept the company's rights over members' names, likenesses and AI-generated voices after the deals end, judged K-pop through a Western lens instead of on its own terms.

The group said major companies run artist care programs, some with in-house medical staff, and sign the government's standard supplementary agreements for minors, covering sleep, education and rest. Fairness, it argued, has to be judged with those agreements and Korean law in view, not clause by clause.

It also objected to contract details from an ongoing legal dispute being disclosed to foreign media despite confidentiality obligations, warning that one dispute was being stretched into a verdict on the whole industry. HYBE and ADOR had responded a day earlier, saying the contracts were lawful and negotiated in good faith.
items.socialCaption: K-pop's industry body says don't call it 'oppressive control', its new statement defends the training system behind the music.
items.seoDescription: The Korea Popmusic Industry Association has rejected the idea that K-pop is defined by oppressive control, pushing back on the New York Times' NewJeans contract report.

body: Nearly 7,000 people from across Asia gathered in Goyang, South Korea, on October 24 for AIA's 'K-Pop Together, Give Together' concert, the insurer's first cross-market event and its largest regional gathering to date.
The lineup brought together K-pop icons PSY, J.Y. Park, ITZY, CHUNG HA and JINUSEAN, with Korean broadcaster Jae Min Park and Girls' Generation member Tiffany Young hosting the night.

More than 300 Filipino customers, agents and partners flew in for the show, joining guests from South Korea, Malaysia and Singapore. Beyond the concert, guests explored Korean culture through a K-Beauty color analysis, found their names written in Hangul, and took home exclusive AIA light sticks.

The event also carried a giving angle: each participating market partnered with a local charity, and AIA Philippines chose Kythe Foundation, which supports children with chronic illnesses and their families. It ties into AIA One Billion, the company's push to inspire one billion people across Asia to live healthier lives by 2030.

AIA Korea chief marketing officer Ji-Ye Hwang and AIA Philippines president and chief executive Melita Teo both attended, with Teo saying the gathering showed how shared experiences can unite communities and strengthen relationships across markets.
